I need to understand how archiving works for projects, issues, and comments.

Two archiving bugs surfaced. Archived issues vanish from search but their comments remain discoverable and link to the archived issue. Archiving a project hides it from search yet its issues and comments stay searchable regardless of whether the admin archived them too.

Restoring an archived project never brings it back into search, and neither do the issues or comments that were kept. A search index rebuild job was run to clean this up, but it made things worse: archived issues, deleted comments, and archived project content all resurfaced. In a large workspace, older issues and their comments remained missing after the rebuild, while irrelevant entries survived.

Search visibility is governed by a strict three-tier rule. A project appears only while live. An issue appears only while both the issue and its project are live. A comment appears only while the comment, its issue, and that issue's project are all live. This rule must hold through archiving, restoring, and any edits or comments made afterward.

A workspace rebuild must leave only entries permitted by the visibility rule and must not touch other workspaces. The bugs are now isolated to two specific gaps: archived issues fail to purge their comments from the index, and archiving a project fails to remove its issues and comments even when those items were not archived separately.

Restored projects must be re-indexed so they return to search. Issues and comments that were kept during archiving must also be re-indexed on restore. Archived issues and their comments should remain hidden.

The rebuild job only fetches the first page of results because it uses a null cursor, which explains why older issues and comments remain missing in large workspaces. It also upserts new entries without deleting stale ones, so archived content and deleted comments survive the rebuild. I still need to check whether comment updates trigger re-indexing.

I need to understand comment, issue, and project updates. I also need to understand how listing works with pagination.

I need to check if comment.updated and project.updated events exist. The search service needs listener fixes, and the reindex job needs rebuild fixes. I also need to verify whether comments store projectId, since the current index sets it to null.

`updateComment` does not emit an event.

`comment.created` indexes comments even when the project is archived. `issue.updated` reindexes issues even when the project is archived. Comment edits do not emit events, so they would not update the search index.

`updateProject` does not emit an event, so project content updates would not refresh the search index. The bug report does not specifically mention project updates.

The activity service records "comment.updated" as an activity type, but it is not a domain event. This suggests a missing bridge between comment updates and search re-indexing.

Archiving a project removes it from search, but its issues and comments remain indexed. The fix is to purge all issues and comments of that project from the search index when `project.archived` fires.

Indexing an issue or comment must also verify both the issue and the parent project are live.

`updateIssue` and `createComment` only check that the issue itself is not archived. They do not verify the parent project is live. This allows edits to live issues inside archived projects, and comments to be posted on those issues, which would incorrectly update the search index.
